title: Unsound type assertion silently breaks at runtime

hints.title: Where to look
hints.body: Open `src/userLoader.ts` and find the `loadUser` function. Notice the line `const user = data as User`. TypeScript accepts this without complaint, but it is a *lie* to the compiler — it asserts that whatever came back from the API is definitely a `User`, without verifying a single field. If the API returns `null`, `{}`, or an object with a missing `email`, the next line `user.email.toLowerCase()` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime.

hints.title: The concept
hints.body: This is an **unsound type assertion** (sometimes called an "unsafe cast"). TypeScript's `as T` keyword tells the compiler to *trust you* — it performs zero runtime validation. Type safety in TypeScript is only as strong as the validation you do at the boundary where `unknown`/external data enters your program. The correct fix is a **type guard**: a function that accepts `unknown` and returns `data is User`, checking every required field at runtime before the cast is made.

hints.title: The fix approach

badPatches.title: try/catch around the unsound cast
